records.issue_text: Trailing-slash/empty-path edge case unaddressed: for http://example.com/ with matching host, website_name becomes 'example.com/' showing a dangling slash where old UI showed clean 'example.com', with no test covering same-domain website with empty or '/' path
records.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, when `website_host == discourse_host` it returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. For `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `"/"`, so `website_name` becomes `"example.com/"`. The old client-side `websiteName` (`website.split("/")[2]`) would have displayed `"example.com"` without the trailing slash, so this diff introduces a visible formatting regression for the root/empty-path case. The added specs cover `/user` but do not cover `"/"` or empty path on same-domain.

records.issue_text: Sibling subdomain branch (elsif) in user_serializer.rb:141 shows full URL path for websites on different subdomains (e.g. forum.example.com vs shop.example.com), violating the stated intent of full path only for same domain
records.rationale: The diff doesn’t state an intent of “full path only for same domain.” In fact, the new logic explicitly treats sibling subdomains as a case where it may include the path: the `elsif` branch is commented `# www.example.com == forum.example.com` and, when the parent domains match, returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` (i.e., includes the path even when subdomains differ). This contradicts the finding’s claim about the stated intent.

records.issue_text: include_website_name returns true while website_name can be nil (e.g. malformed website values), leaving an always-null website_name key in the JSON payload due to inconsistent predicates
records.rationale: In `UserSerializer`, `include_website_name` returns `website.present?`, but `website_name` can explicitly return `nil` when parsing fails or yields no host (`website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil; return if website_host.nil?`). For malformed-but-present website strings, this mismatch will include the `website_name` attribute while its value is `nil`, producing a `website_name: null` key in the JSON payload.
